title: Lisa Su Praises Jensen Huang as Outstanding, Then Urges AMD to Ignore the Noise

content_html:
On Tuesday (the 17th), U.S. Eastern Time, at the TomorrowX Summit held in Austin, Texas, AMD chief Lisa Su directly addressed the rival-related topic that has been heatedly discussed recently—Nvidia had just parted ways with former CEO Jensen Huang last week, and the controversy had not yet subsided. She did not sidestep it: “Nvidia is a remarkable company, and Jensen Huang has been an outstanding leader driving the development of the entire industry.” Given that the two companies have been locked in close combat for years, this public affirmation seems quite rare.

“The noise will dissipate on its own over time”After praising the rival, she quickly steered the conversation back to her own company’s strategy. Lisa Su acknowledged that too much is happening in the industry right now, but whether from AMD’s perspective or the industry’s as a whole, it is necessary to appropriately pull attention away from all the distractions—“these noises will eventually dissipate on their own over time.” Recently, the controversy over Jensen Huang’s resignation and possible return is dominating market attention, and her remarks sounded more like setting the tone internally: don’t be led around by outside drama.

The real opportunity is at the infrastructure siteAs for where AMD should focus its efforts, her answer was very specific: the company currently has enormous development opportunities, and the key is to join this large-scale infrastructure buildout, work with partners to advance the future product roadmap, and ultimately meet or even exceed market expectations. While generously acknowledging the rival’s industry position and reining the competitive narrative back to execution, Lisa Su’s stance was this: AMD’s decisive factor is not in a war of words, but in whether it can deliver products on schedule.
